import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
from pathlib import Path

# Make tables easier to inspect in Jupyter
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 50)
pd.set_option("display.width", 160)

# Use cleaned CSVs; identifiers stay strings to preserve leading zeros.
DATA_DIR = Path(".")
READ_OPTIONS = {
    "dtype": {
        "sPropCode": "string",
        "sUnitCode": "string",
        "sSite": "string",
        "hUnit": "string",
    }
}
listings = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "clean_equinoxe_listings.csv", **READ_OPTIONS)
leases = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "clean_equinoxe_lease_history.csv", **READ_OPTIONS)
concessions = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "clean_equinoxe_concessions.csv", **READ_OPTIONS)
asking = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "clean_equinoxe_asking_history.csv", **READ_OPTIONS)

# Parse date fields explicitly after loading.
for col in ["sLeaseFrom", "sLeaseTo", "sSignDate", "sAvailable"]:
    if col in leases.columns:
        leases[col] = pd.to_datetime(leases[col], errors="coerce")
for col in ["sAsOf", "sAvailable"]:
    if col in listings.columns:
        listings[col] = pd.to_datetime(listings[col], errors="coerce")
for col in ["sDateFrom", "sDateTo"]:
    if col in concessions.columns:
        concessions[col] = pd.to_datetime(concessions[col], errors="coerce")
if "sMonth" in asking.columns:
    asking["sMonth"] = pd.to_datetime(asking["sMonth"], errors="coerce")
    asking["date"] = asking["sMonth"]
if "sLeaseFrom" in leases.columns:
    leases["year"] = leases["sLeaseFrom"].dt.year

tables = {
    "listings": listings,
    "leases": leases,
    "concessions": concessions,
    "asking": asking
}

# Inspect each dataset
for name, df in tables.items():
    print(f"\\n--- {name.upper()} ---")
    print("Shape:", df.shape)
    print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())
    display(df.head(3))

print("Data loaded from cleaned CSVs; identifier strings and dates prepared.")

def require_columns(df, columns, df_name="DataFrame"):
    """Check that required columns are available."""
    missing = [col for col in columns if col not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        print(f"{df_name} is missing columns: {missing}")
        return False
    return True

def numeric_series(df, col):
    """Convert a column to numeric values without changing the source file."""
    return pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

def finish_plot():
    """Apply consistent formatting and show the current Matplotlib figure."""
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

def show_empty_message(message):
    print("Chart skipped:", message)

#3.Rent distribution by building    
if require_columns(listings, ["sBuilding", "sRent"], "listings"):
    plot_data = listings[["sBuilding", "sRent"]].copy()
    plot_data["sRent"] = numeric_series(plot_data, "sRent")
    plot_data = plot_data.dropna()

    buildings = sorted(plot_data["sBuilding"].unique())
    rent_groups = [
        plot_data.loc[plot_data["sBuilding"] == b, "sRent"].values
        for b in buildings
    ]

    plt.figure(figsize=(11, 5))
    plt.boxplot(rent_groups, tick_labels=buildings, showfliers=True)
    plt.title("Listed Rent Distribution by Building")
    plt.xlabel("Building")
    plt.ylabel("Monthly listed rent ($)")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
    finish_plot()

#Rent comparisons
#5.Asking,contractual, and effective rent over time
# Column settings confirmed from the CSV schema
ASKING_RENT_COL = "sAskingRent"
# Set the correct asking rent column above before running.
if ASKING_RENT_COL is None:
    show_empty_message("Set ASKING_RENT_COL using the asking.columns output.")
elif not require_columns(asking, ["date", ASKING_RENT_COL], "asking"):
    pass
elif not require_columns(leases, ["year", "sRent"], "leases"):
    pass
else:
    asking_plot = asking[["date", ASKING_RENT_COL]].copy()
    asking_plot["year"] = asking_plot["date"].dt.year
    asking_plot["asking_rent"] = numeric_series(
        asking_plot, ASKING_RENT_COL
    )
    asking_year = asking_plot.groupby("year")["asking_rent"].median()

    lease_plot = leases.copy()
    lease_plot["sRent"] = numeric_series(lease_plot, "sRent")
    contractual_year = lease_plot.groupby("year")["sRent"].median()

    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
    plt.plot(
        asking_year.index, asking_year.values,
        marker="o", label="Asking rent"
    )
    plt.plot(
        contractual_year.index, contractual_year.values,
        marker="o", label="Contractual rent"
    )

    if "sRentEffective" in leases.columns:
        lease_plot["sRentEffective"] = numeric_series(
            lease_plot, "sRentEffective"
        )
        effective_year = lease_plot.groupby("year")[
            "sRentEffective"
        ].median()
        plt.plot(
            effective_year.index, effective_year.values,
            marker="o", label="Effective rent"
        )

    plt.title("Annual Median Asking and Lease Rents")
    plt.xlabel("Year")
    plt.ylabel("Monthly rent ($)")
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    finish_plot()

#6 Contractual vs effective rent by year
if require_columns(
    leases, ["year", "sRent", "sRentEffective"], "leases"
):
    rent_data = leases.copy()
    rent_data["sRent"] = numeric_series(rent_data, "sRent")
    rent_data["sRentEffective"] = numeric_series(
        rent_data, "sRentEffective"
    )

    yearly = rent_data.groupby("year").agg(
        contractual=("sRent", "median"),
        effective=("sRentEffective", "median")
    ).dropna()

    ax = yearly.plot(kind="bar", figsize=(10, 5))
    ax.set_title("Contractual vs. Effective Rent by Year")
    ax.set_xlabel("Lease start year")
    ax.set_ylabel("Monthly rent ($)")
    ax.legend(["Contractual rent", "Effective rent"])
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=0)
    finish_plot()

    yearly["gap_pct"] = (
        (yearly["effective"] / yearly["contractual"]) - 1
    ) * 100
    display(yearly.round(2))
else:
    show_empty_message(
        "The lease file must contain year, sRent, and sRentEffective."
    )

#7.Asking rent vs. contractual rent
if ASKING_RENT_COL is None:
    show_empty_message("Set ASKING_RENT_COL first.")
elif require_columns(asking, ["date", ASKING_RENT_COL], "asking") and \
     require_columns(leases, ["year", "sRent"], "leases"):
    a = asking[["date", ASKING_RENT_COL]].copy()
    a["year"] = a["date"].dt.year
    a["asking_rent"] = numeric_series(a, ASKING_RENT_COL)
    a = a.groupby("year")["asking_rent"].median().rename("asking")

    l = leases[["year", "sRent"]].copy()
    l["sRent"] = numeric_series(l, "sRent")
    l = l.groupby("year")["sRent"].median().rename("contractual")

    comparison = pd.concat([a, l], axis=1).dropna()

    plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))
    plt.scatter(comparison["asking"], comparison["contractual"])

    low = comparison.min().min()
    high = comparison.max().max()
    plt.plot([low, high], [low, high], linestyle="--")

    for year, row in comparison.iterrows():
        plt.annotate(str(year), (row["asking"], row["contractual"]))

    plt.title("Annual Median Asking vs. Contractual Rent")
    plt.xlabel("Median asking rent ($)")
    plt.ylabel("Median contractual rent ($)")
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    finish_plot()

#Same-unit rent growth
# Prefer hUnit if it is available and consistent in the lease file.
# Otherwise, use the project-prescribed property + unit code.
if "hUnit" in leases.columns and leases["hUnit"].notna().all():
    UNIT_KEY = ["hUnit"]
elif require_columns(
    leases, ["sPropCode", "sUnitCode"], "leases"
):
    UNIT_KEY = ["sPropCode", "sUnitCode"]
else:
    UNIT_KEY = None

if UNIT_KEY is not None and require_columns(
    leases, ["sLeaseFrom", "sRent"], "leases"
):
    pairs = leases.copy()
    pairs["sLeaseFrom"] = pd.to_datetime(
        pairs["sLeaseFrom"], errors="coerce"
    )
    pairs["sRent"] = numeric_series(pairs, "sRent")
    pairs = pairs.dropna(subset=UNIT_KEY + ["sLeaseFrom", "sRent"])
    pairs = pairs.sort_values(UNIT_KEY + ["sLeaseFrom"])

    # Prior lease values within the same unit
    pairs["prev_rent"] = pairs.groupby(UNIT_KEY)["sRent"].shift(1)
    pairs["prev_date"] = pairs.groupby(UNIT_KEY)["sLeaseFrom"].shift(1)

    # Time between consecutive lease start dates
    pairs["gap_years"] = (
        (pairs["sLeaseFrom"] - pairs["prev_date"]).dt.days / 365.25
    )

    # Keep plausible lease-to-lease comparisons
    pairs = pairs[
        pairs["gap_years"].between(0.5, 2.5, inclusive="neither")
    ].copy()

    pairs = pairs[
        (pairs["prev_rent"] > 0) &
        (pairs["sRent"] > 0)
    ].copy()

    # Annualized rent growth
    pairs["growth_pct"] = (
        (pairs["sRent"] / pairs["prev_rent"]) **
        (1 / pairs["gap_years"]) - 1
    ) * 100

    pairs["year"] = pairs["sLeaseFrom"].dt.year

    print("Usable same-unit lease pairs:", len(pairs))
    display(pairs.head())
else:
    pairs = pd.DataFrame()
    show_empty_message("Could not identify a valid unit key and rent/date fields.")

#8.Same-unit growth vs. overrall median grown
if not pairs.empty and require_columns(leases, ["year", "sRent"], "leases"):
    # Overall median rent growth by lease start year
    overall = leases.copy()
    overall["sRent"] = numeric_series(overall, "sRent")
    overall_median = overall.groupby("year")["sRent"].median()
    overall_growth = overall_median.pct_change() * 100

    # Same-unit median annualized growth
    same_unit_growth = pairs.groupby("year")["growth_pct"].median()

    comparison = pd.DataFrame({
        "Overall median rent growth": overall_growth,
        "Same-unit median growth": same_unit_growth
    }).dropna()

    ax = comparison.plot(
        kind="line", marker="o", figsize=(10, 5)
    )
    ax.set_title("Overall Rent Growth vs. Same-Unit Rent Growth")
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
    ax.set_ylabel("Annual rent growth (%)")
    ax.axhline(0, linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
    ax.legend()
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    finish_plot()
    display(comparison.round(2))
else:
    show_empty_message("Create usable same-unit pairs first.")

    plt.title("Rent per Square Foot by Unit Type")
    plt.xlabel("Unit type")
    plt.ylabel("Monthly rent per square foot ($)")

<h1 id="Part-2-%E2%80%94-Province-and-lease-type-breakdowns,-2026-estimate,-backtest,-external-context">Part 2 — Province and lease-type breakdowns, 2026 estimate, backtest, external context¶</h1><p>What this part does. It takes the same-unit lease pairs built earlier (cell "Same-unit rent growth"), attaches a province and a renewal/turnover label to every pair, checks the pair table for duplicates and gaps, and then builds the 2026 estimates, the backtest and the external-data comparison.</p> <p>Matching rule (how a "pair" is formed).</p>
  • A pair is two consecutive leases on the same unit, ordered by lease start date. The unit key is hUnit (fallback: property code + unit code).
  • The pair is kept only if the gap between the two lease start dates is more than 0.5 and less than 2.5 years and both rents are positive. This drops missed records and overlapping or very long gaps.
  • Each later lease is paired with the single lease immediately before it, so no lease is used as the "later" side twice.
  • The pair is assigned to the year the later lease starts.
  • Province comes from the building (The Met = Ontario; the other five buildings = Québec).
  • Renewal vs turnover is taken from the later lease's sRenewal flag (1 = renewal, 0 = turnover). The earlier lease's flag is not used.
<p>Annualization. growth_pct = ((later rent / earlier rent) ** (1 / years_between) − 1) × 100, with years_between = days between start dates / 365.25. Most gaps are almost exactly one year, so annualization mainly matters for the minority of pairs with a shorter or longer gap.</p> <p>Concessions. All growth figures use the contractual rent (sRent), not the effective rent after concessions. Free rent, free parking and promotional credits are therefore not netted out. Earlier cells compare contractual and effective rent by year; an effective-rent version of the pair table needs the lease file (see the notes at the end).</p>
In [15]:
# ---- Build the province / lease-type pair table --------------------------
BUILDING_PROVINCE = {
    "The Met": "Ontario",
    "Daniel-Johnson": "Quebec",
    "Le Carlyle": "Quebec",
    "Levesque": "Quebec",
    "Saint-Elzear": "Quebec",
    "Westpark": "Quebec",
}
LEASE_TYPE_FROM_FLAG = {1: "Renewal", 0: "Turnover"}
EXPORTED_PAIR_FILES = [
    "ontario_renewals.csv", "ontario_turnovers.csv",
    "quebec_renewals.csv", "quebec_turnovers.csv",
]

def pairs_from_notebook(p):
    """Standardize the in-memory `pairs` table (one row per later lease)."""
    if "hUnit" in p.columns:
        unit = p["hUnit"].astype("string")
    else:
        unit = p["sPropCode"].astype("string") + "-" + p["sUnitCode"].astype("string")
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "building": p["sBuilding"].astype("string"),
        "unit_id": unit,
        "prior_start": p["prev_date"],
        "current_start": p["sLeaseFrom"],
        "prior_rent": p["prev_rent"],
        "current_rent": p["sRent"],
        "years_between": p["gap_years"],
        "growth_pct": p["growth_pct"],
        "year": p["year"],
        "current_renewal_flag": pd.to_numeric(p["sRenewal"], errors="coerce"),
        "file_province": pd.NA,
        "file_lease_type": pd.NA,
    }).reset_index(drop=True)

def pairs_from_exported_files(data_dir):
    """Standardize the four exported province x lease-type pair files."""
    dtypes = {"unit_id": "string", "unit_code": "string", "property_code": "string"}
    raw = pd.concat(
        [pd.read_csv(Path(data_dir) / f, dtype=dtypes) for f in EXPORTED_PAIR_FILES],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "building": raw["building"].astype("string"),
        "unit_id": raw["unit_id"],
        "prior_start": pd.to_datetime(raw["prior_sLeaseFrom"]),
        "current_start": pd.to_datetime(raw["current_sLeaseFrom"]),
        "prior_rent": raw["prior_sRent"],
        "current_rent": raw["current_sRent"],
        "years_between": raw["years_between"],
        "growth_pct": raw["growth_pct"],
        "year": raw["year"],
        "current_renewal_flag": pd.to_numeric(raw["current_sRenewal"], errors="coerce"),
        "file_province": raw["province"],
        "file_lease_type": raw["lease_type"],
    })

_notebook_pairs_ok = (
    "pairs" in globals() and isinstance(pairs, pd.DataFrame)
    and not pairs.empty and {"sBuilding", "prev_rent", "gap_years"} <= set(pairs.columns)
)
if _notebook_pairs_ok:
    base = pairs_from_notebook(pairs)
    PAIR_SOURCE = "in-memory `pairs` from the same-unit growth cell"
else:
    base = pairs_from_exported_files(DATA_DIR)
    PAIR_SOURCE = "the four exported province x lease-type pair files"

pairs_all = base.assign(
    province=base["building"].map(BUILDING_PROVINCE),
    lease_type=base["current_renewal_flag"].astype("Int64").map(LEASE_TYPE_FROM_FLAG),
)
pairs_all["province"] = pairs_all["province"].astype("object")
pairs_all["lease_type"] = pairs_all["lease_type"].astype("object")
print(f"Pair source: {PAIR_SOURCE}")
print(f"Pairs: {len(pairs_all):,}")

# Optional cross-checks when the other sources are also available
if _notebook_pairs_ok and all((Path(DATA_DIR) / f).exists() for f in EXPORTED_PAIR_FILES):
    other = pairs_from_exported_files(DATA_DIR)
    other = other.assign(province=other["building"].map(BUILDING_PROVINCE),
                         lease_type=other["current_renewal_flag"].astype("Int64").map(LEASE_TYPE_FROM_FLAG))
    key = ["province", "lease_type", "year"]
    a = pairs_all.groupby(key).size()
    b = other.groupby(key).size()
    diff = pd.concat([a.rename("notebook"), b.rename("exported_files")], axis=1).fillna(0)
    print("Notebook pairs vs exported files — groups with different counts:",
          int((diff["notebook"] != diff["exported_files"]).sum()))
if "listings" in globals() and "sState" in listings.columns:
    listing_province = listings.groupby("sBuilding")["sState"].agg(lambda s: s.mode().iat[0])
    mismatches = {b: (BUILDING_PROVINCE.get(b), s) for b, s in listing_province.items()
                  if BUILDING_PROVINCE.get(b) != s}
    print("Building->province mapping vs listings.sState mismatches:", mismatches or "none")

display(
    pairs_all.groupby(["province", "building"]).size().rename("pairs").reset_index()
)

# ---- Integrity checks: unmatched, duplicate and implausible pairs ----------
def validate_pairs(df):
    checks = []
    def add(name, ok, detail=""):
        checks.append({"check": name, "passed": bool(ok), "detail": detail})

    add("Every building maps to a province", df["province"].notna().all(),
        f"unmapped buildings: {sorted(df.loc[df['province'].isna(), 'building'].unique())}")
    add("Every pair is a Renewal or a Turnover", df["lease_type"].isin(["Renewal", "Turnover"]).all(),
        f"unlabelled pairs: {int(df['lease_type'].isna().sum())}")
    add("No fully duplicated rows", not df.duplicated().any(), f"{int(df.duplicated().sum())} duplicates")
    add("Each later lease used once (unit + current start)",
        not df.duplicated(["unit_id", "current_start"]).any(),
        f"{int(df.duplicated(['unit_id', 'current_start']).sum())} repeats")
    add("Each earlier lease used once (unit + prior start)",
        not df.duplicated(["unit_id", "prior_start"]).any(),
        f"{int(df.duplicated(['unit_id', 'prior_start']).sum())} repeats")
    add("Each unit belongs to one building and one province",
        (df.groupby("unit_id")["building"].nunique() == 1).all()
        and (df.groupby("building")["province"].nunique() == 1).all())
    add("Later lease starts after earlier lease",
        (df["current_start"] > df["prior_start"]).all())
    add("Gap between starts within (0.5, 2.5) years",
        df["years_between"].between(0.5, 2.5, inclusive="neither").all(),
        f"min {df['years_between'].min():.2f}, max {df['years_between'].max():.2f}")
    add("Both rents positive", ((df["prior_rent"] > 0) & (df["current_rent"] > 0)).all())
    recomputed = ((df["current_rent"] / df["prior_rent"]) ** (1 / df["years_between"]) - 1) * 100
    add("growth_pct recomputes from the two rents", (recomputed - df["growth_pct"]).abs().max() < 1e-6,
        f"max abs difference {(recomputed - df['growth_pct']).abs().max():.2e}")
    add("Pair year equals year of later lease start",
        (df["current_start"].dt.year == df["year"]).all())
    add("growth_pct is finite", np.isfinite(df["growth_pct"]).all())
    if df["file_province"].notna().any():
        add("Mapped province agrees with the exported file's province",
            (df["province"] == df["file_province"]).all())
        add("Later-lease flag agrees with the exported file's lease type",
            (df["lease_type"] == df["file_lease_type"]).all())
    out = pd.DataFrame(checks)
    return out

check_table = validate_pairs(pairs_all)
display(check_table)
assert check_table["passed"].all(), "At least one integrity check failed — see table above."

# Plausibility of counts (information only)
counts = (pairs_all.groupby(["year", "province", "lease_type"]).size()
          .unstack(["province", "lease_type"]).fillna(0).astype(int))
counts["Total"] = counts.sum(axis=1)
print("Pairs per later-lease start year, by province and lease type:")
display(counts)

near_one_year = (pairs_all["years_between"] - 1).abs() <= 0.05
print(f"Share of pairs whose gap is within 0.05 years of one year: {near_one_year.mean():.1%} "
      f"(annualization matters mainly for the other {1 - near_one_year.mean():.1%}).")
print(f"Growth outside [-10%, +30%]: {int((~pairs_all['growth_pct'].between(-10, 30)).sum())} pairs; "
      f"range {pairs_all['growth_pct'].min():.1f}% to {pairs_all['growth_pct'].max():.1f}%.")
first_year = pairs_all.groupby("province")["year"].min()
print("First pair year by province:", first_year.to_dict(),
      "-> Ontario has no matched pairs before the later lease starts in 2024.")

# Compare with lease counts when the lease table is loaded
if "leases" in globals() and {"sBuilding", "year"} <= set(leases.columns):
    lease_counts = (leases.assign(province=leases["sBuilding"].map(BUILDING_PROVINCE))
                    .groupby(["year", "province"]).size().rename("leases_starting"))
    pair_counts = pairs_all.groupby(["year", "province"]).size().rename("pairs")
    cmp_counts = pd.concat([lease_counts, pair_counts], axis=1).fillna(0).astype(int)
    cmp_counts["leases_without_pair"] = cmp_counts["leases_starting"] - cmp_counts["pairs"]
    print("Leases starting vs pairs (leases without a pair = first lease on a unit or gap outside 0.5-2.5 years):")
    display(cmp_counts.loc[cmp_counts.index.get_level_values(0) >= 2020])
    assert (cmp_counts["pairs"] <= cmp_counts["leases_starting"]).all(), "More pairs than leases in some year."

<h2 id="estimate_2026()-%E2%80%94-recent-history-estimate-with-uncertainty">estimate_2026() — recent-history estimate with uncertainty¶</h2><p>Method (deliberately simple so every number can be traced).</p>
  1. Take matched pairs whose later lease starts in 2023, 2024 or 2025.
  2. Within each segment, compute the median annualized growth for each year (a year counts only if it has at least 15 pairs).
  3. The central estimate is the average of those yearly medians, so each year has equal weight. This stops the many 2024–2025 leases from swamping 2023.
  4. The range is the lowest and highest yearly median (year-to-year spread). The pooled median and the 25th–75th percentile of individual pairs are shown alongside, so the spread between leases is visible too.
  5. Segments with fewer than two usable years or fewer than 50 pairs get no estimate. Segments with fewer than three years or fewer than 100 pairs carry a caution flag.
<p>Segments are the whole portfolio, each province, renewals vs turnovers across both provinces, and the four province × lease-type groups. The range is a historical spread, not a statistical confidence interval.</p>
In [18]:
SEGMENTS = [("All", "All"), ("Ontario", "All"), ("Quebec", "All"),
            ("All", "Renewal"), ("All", "Turnover"),
            ("Ontario", "Renewal"), ("Ontario", "Turnover"),
            ("Quebec", "Renewal"), ("Quebec", "Turnover")]

def segment_pairs(pairs, province, lease_type, growth_col="growth_pct",
                  province_col="province", type_col="lease_type"):
    """Rows of one segment with a finite growth value ('All' = no filter)."""
    mask = pairs[growth_col].notna() & np.isfinite(pairs[growth_col])
    if province != "All":
        mask &= pairs[province_col] == province
    if lease_type != "All":
        mask &= pairs[type_col] == lease_type
    return pairs.loc[mask]

def annual_medians(df, years, growth_col="growth_pct", year_col="year", min_pairs_per_year=15):
    """Median growth and pair count per year; years below the minimum are dropped."""
    sub = df[df[year_col].isin(list(years))]
    g = sub.groupby(year_col)[growth_col].agg(median="median", n="size")
    return g[g["n"] >= min_pairs_per_year]

def estimate_2026(pairs, growth_col="growth_pct", year_col="year",
                  start_year=2023, end_year=2025,
                  min_pairs_per_year=15, min_years=2, min_total_pairs=50,
                  caution_pairs=100):
    """
    Recent-history estimate for end_year + 1, one row per segment.
    Central estimate = mean of yearly medians over start_year..end_year.
    Range = lowest / highest yearly median. Pooled median and the 25th-75th
    percentile of individual pairs are reported for context.
    """
    years = range(start_year, end_year + 1)
    rows = []
    for province, lease_type in SEGMENTS:
        seg = segment_pairs(pairs, province, lease_type, growth_col)
        hist = seg[seg[year_col].isin(years)]
        am = annual_medians(seg, years, growth_col, year_col, min_pairs_per_year)
        n_total = int(am["n"].sum()) if not am.empty else 0
        row = {
            "forecast_year": end_year + 1, "province": province, "lease_type": lease_type,
            "method": f"Mean of yearly medians, {start_year}-{end_year}",
            "years_used": ", ".join(str(int(y)) for y in am.index),
            "annual_medians_pct": "; ".join(f"{int(y)}: {m:.2f}" for y, m in am["median"].items()),
            "n_pairs": n_total,
            "n_by_year": "; ".join(f"{int(y)}: {int(n)}" for y, n in am["n"].items()),
        }
        if len(am) < min_years or n_total < min_total_pairs:
            row.update({"estimate_pct": np.nan, "range_low_pct": np.nan, "range_high_pct": np.nan,
                        "pooled_median_pct": np.nan, "pair_p25_pct": np.nan, "pair_p75_pct": np.nan,
                        "note": f"No estimate: needs >= {min_years} years and >= {min_total_pairs} pairs"})
        else:
            used = hist[hist[year_col].isin(am.index)][growth_col]
            notes = []
            if len(am) < len(list(years)):
                notes.append(f"history limited to {len(am)} year(s)")
            if n_total < caution_pairs:
                notes.append(f"small sample (n={n_total}); indicative only")
            row.update({
                "estimate_pct": float(am["median"].mean()),
                "range_low_pct": float(am["median"].min()),
                "range_high_pct": float(am["median"].max()),
                "pooled_median_pct": float(used.median()),
                "pair_p25_pct": float(used.quantile(0.25)),
                "pair_p75_pct": float(used.quantile(0.75)),
                "note": "; ".join(notes) if notes else "ok",
            })
        rows.append(row)
    cols = ["forecast_year", "province", "lease_type", "method", "estimate_pct",
            "range_low_pct", "range_high_pct", "pooled_median_pct", "pair_p25_pct", "pair_p75_pct",
            "n_pairs", "n_by_year", "annual_medians_pct", "years_used", "note"]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)[cols]

forecast_2026 = estimate_2026(pairs_all)
display(forecast_2026.round(2))

<h2 id="backtest()-%E2%80%94-would-this-method-have-worked-in-2023,-2024-and-2025?">backtest() — would this method have worked in 2023, 2024 and 2025?¶</h2><p>For each test year the method is applied as if it were run on 1 January of that year: it uses only pairs whose later lease started in the three calendar years before the test year (for 2023: 2020–2022; for 2024: 2021–2023; for 2025: 2022–2024). The function asserts that no training year is on or after the test year. The prediction is compared with the median growth actually observed in the test year.</p> <p>Two simple benchmarks are shown next to it: the original pooled median of every earlier year, and the last-year median (assume next year repeats the last).</p> <p>How to read the results:</p>
  • Segments with fewer than two usable training years are labelled thin and are left out of the summary (Ontario cannot be backtested properly: its first pairs are from 2024).
  • The 2024 and 2025 all-portfolio rows are not like-for-like: the actuals include Ontario, which was not in the older training windows (see the composition column).
  • With only three test years and a few hundred pairs per group, differences between methods are suggestive, not conclusive.
In [19]:
def backtest(pairs, test_years=(2023, 2024, 2025), window=3,
             growth_col="growth_pct", year_col="year",
             min_pairs_per_year=15, min_train_years=2, min_test_pairs=20):
    """
    Walk-forward backtest, one row per segment x test year.
    Training data = pairs whose later lease started in the `window` calendar
    years strictly before the test year. Nothing from the test year or later
    is used to form a prediction.
    """
    rows = []
    for province, lease_type in SEGMENTS:
        seg = segment_pairs(pairs, province, lease_type, growth_col)
        for year in test_years:
            train_years = list(range(year - window, year))
            assert max(train_years) < year, "Training window must end before the test year."
            train_all = seg[seg[year_col] < year]            # for the pooled benchmark only
            train_win = seg[seg[year_col].isin(train_years)]
            test = seg[seg[year_col] == year]
            assert train_win[year_col].max() < year if not train_win.empty else True
            am = annual_medians(seg, train_years, growth_col, year_col, min_pairs_per_year)
            actual = float(test[growth_col].median()) if not test.empty else np.nan
            row = {
                "province": province, "lease_type": lease_type, "year": year,
                "training_years": f"{min(train_years)}-{max(train_years)}",
                "training_years_used": len(am), "training_pairs": int(am["n"].sum()) if len(am) else 0,
                "predicted_pct": float(am["median"].mean()) if len(am) else np.nan,
                "range_low_pct": float(am["median"].min()) if len(am) else np.nan,
                "range_high_pct": float(am["median"].max()) if len(am) else np.nan,
                "actual_pct": actual, "comparisons": int(len(test)),
                "bench_pooled_median_pct": float(train_all[growth_col].median()) if len(train_all) else np.nan,
                "bench_last_year_pct": (float(seg.loc[seg[year_col] == year - 1, growth_col].median())
                                        if (seg[year_col] == year - 1).sum() >= min_pairs_per_year else np.nan),
            }
            row["error_pct_points"] = row["predicted_pct"] - actual
            row["in_range"] = (bool(row["range_low_pct"] <= actual <= row["range_high_pct"])
                               if len(am) >= 2 and not np.isnan(actual) else pd.NA)
            new_provs = set(test["province"]) - set(train_win["province"]) if len(test) else set()
            row["composition_note"] = ("test year includes " + "/".join(sorted(new_provs)) + " not in training"
                                       if new_provs else "")
            if len(am) == 0:
                row["status"] = "no usable history"
            elif len(am) < min_train_years:
                row["status"] = f"thin: {len(am)} training year"
            elif len(test) < min_test_pairs:
                row["status"] = "small test sample"
            else:
                row["status"] = "ok"
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def summarize_backtest(bt):
    """Mean absolute error per segment over rows with status 'ok' only."""
    ok = bt[bt["status"] == "ok"].copy()
    ok["abs_err_method"] = ok["error_pct_points"].abs()
    ok["abs_err_pooled"] = (ok["bench_pooled_median_pct"] - ok["actual_pct"]).abs()
    ok["abs_err_last"] = (ok["bench_last_year_pct"] - ok["actual_pct"]).abs()
    out = ok.groupby(["province", "lease_type"], sort=False).agg(
        test_years_evaluated=("year", "size"),
        mae_method=("abs_err_method", "mean"),
        mae_pooled_median=("abs_err_pooled", "mean"),
        mae_last_year=("abs_err_last", "mean"),
        actual_in_range=("in_range", lambda s: int(s.astype(float).sum())),
    )
    return out.round(2)

backtest_results = backtest(pairs_all)
show_cols = ["province", "lease_type", "year", "training_years", "training_pairs", "predicted_pct",
             "range_low_pct", "range_high_pct", "actual_pct", "error_pct_points", "comparisons",
             "bench_pooled_median_pct", "bench_last_year_pct", "status", "composition_note"]
print("Backtest, whole portfolio and the four province x lease-type groups")
display(backtest_results.loc[
    backtest_results.apply(lambda r: (r["province"], r["lease_type"]) in
                           [("All", "All")] + FOUR_GROUPS, axis=1), show_cols].round(2))
print("Summary over rows with status 'ok' (mean absolute error, percentage points):")
display(summarize_backtest(backtest_results))

# ---- Actual vs predicted growth (backtest) ---------------------------------
def plot_backtest_panel(ax, bt_rows, title):
    bt_rows = bt_rows.sort_values("year")
    ax.plot(bt_rows["year"], bt_rows["actual_pct"], marker="o", label="Actual (median of test-year pairs)")
    pred = bt_rows.dropna(subset=["predicted_pct"])
    if not pred.empty:
        yerr = np.vstack([(pred["predicted_pct"] - pred["range_low_pct"]).clip(lower=0),
                          (pred["range_high_pct"] - pred["predicted_pct"]).clip(lower=0)])
        ax.errorbar(pred["year"], pred["predicted_pct"], yerr=yerr, marker="s", linestyle="--",
                    capsize=4, label="Predicted (mean of prior yearly medians; bar = prior low-high)")
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Test year")
    ax.set_ylabel("Median annualized same-unit growth (%)")
    ax.set_xticks(sorted(bt_rows["year"].unique()))
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.5), sharey=True)
for ax, (prov, lt, ttl) in zip(axes, [("All", "All", "Whole portfolio"),
                                       ("Quebec", "Renewal", "Quebec renewals"),
                                       ("Quebec", "Turnover", "Quebec turnovers")]):
    plot_backtest_panel(ax, backtest_results[(backtest_results["province"] == prov)
                                              & (backtest_results["lease_type"] == lt)], ttl)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
fig.suptitle("Backtest: Actual vs Predicted Rent Growth (2023-2025, trained on prior years only)")
finish_plot()
print("Ontario groups are not charted: their first matched pairs are from 2024, so no test year has two prior training years.")

<h2 id="External-data:-CPI,-CMHC-and-the-regulatory-context">External data: CPI, CMHC and the regulatory context¶</h2><p>Sources used (links kept from the original notes):</p>
  • Statistics Canada CPI, table 18-10-0004-01: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401
  • CMHC Rental Market Survey data tables: https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/housing-markets-data-and-research/housing-data/data-tables/rental-market?ap=a1-p5&linkTo=a1-p1-link1
  • Québec Tribunal administratif du logement (TAL), rent-fixing criteria: https://www.tal.gouv.qc.ca/en/news/?categorie=Fixation+de+loyer+
  • Ontario annual rent increase guideline: https://www.ontario.ca/page/residential-rent-increases
<p>The next cells load the CPI and CMHC files and document exactly what geography, dates and measures they cover, so gaps are visible rather than assumed away.</p> <h3 id="How-each-external-source-is-used">How each external source is used¶</h3> <thead> <th>External source</th> <th>How it is used here</th> <th>Important limitation</th> </thead> <tbody> </tbody> <tbody></tbody>
TAL annual rent-adjustment criteria Explains the Québec regulatory, expense-based context for the forecast. The annual criteria are not a universal rent-increase cap or a direct prediction of this portfolio's changes.
Ontario rent guideline Compared with the Ontario renewal estimates (guideline that applies to most rent-controlled units). The 2026 guideline of 2.1% does not apply to every unit or to turnovers. Exemptions and above-guideline processes matter.
Canada CPI Broad inflation context, including the Shelter component, next to historical rent growth. The uploaded series has no rent-specific CPI category, is Canada-wide, and is incomplete for some calendar years.
CMHC 2023 urban average rents Market-level reference for urban centres only where the geography matches a building. Average rent levels are not rent growth for the same unit, and 2023 is a single-year reference.
CMHC vacancy rates Descriptive context on market conditions where comparable urban data exists. 2024–2025 vacancy rates were not located and are not inferred or interpolated.
<p>The 2024 and 2025 CMHC urban datasets could not be located, so those years are documented as missing rather than forced into the analysis. The 2025 rural workbook is described below but is not treated as a comparable for urban buildings.</p>

# ---- Statistics Canada CPI: load and document coverage --------------------
import csv, re

def find_file(patterns, folder=DATA_DIR):
    for pat in patterns:
        hits = sorted(Path(folder).glob(pat))
        if hits:
            return hits[0]
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No file matching {patterns} in {Path(folder).resolve()}")

def load_statcan_cpi(path):
    """Parse the Statistics Canada CPI extract (title block, month header, measure rows)."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    meta = {"release": next((r[0] for r in rows if r and r[0].startswith("Release date")), ""),
            "table": next((r[0] for r in rows if r and r[0].startswith("Table:")), "")}
    geo_row = next(r for r in rows if r and r[0] == "Geography" and len(r) > 1)
    meta["geography"] = geo_row[1]
    hdr = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and r[0].startswith("Products and product groups"))
    months = pd.to_datetime([m for m in rows[hdr][1:] if m], format="%B %Y")
    base = rows[hdr + 1][1] if len(rows[hdr + 1]) > 1 else ""
    meta["base"] = base
    records = []
    for r in rows[hdr + 2:]:
        if not r or not r[0].strip() or r[0].startswith("Footnotes"):
            break
        name = re.sub(r"(\s+\d+)+$", "", r[0].strip())
        for m, v in zip(months, r[1:]):
            records.append({"measure": name, "month": m, "index": pd.to_numeric(v, errors="coerce")})
    return pd.DataFrame(records), meta

cpi_path = find_file(["Consumer*Price*Index*.csv"])
cpi_long, cpi_meta = load_statcan_cpi(cpi_path)
cpi_long["year"] = cpi_long["month"].dt.year

all_months = pd.date_range(cpi_long["month"].min(), cpi_long["month"].max(), freq="MS")
missing_months = sorted(set(all_months) - set(cpi_long["month"]))
coverage_cpi = pd.DataFrame({
    "Item": ["File", "Geography in this extract", "Measures in file", "First month", "Last month",
             "Months present", "Gaps inside range", "Index base", "Release date (as stated in file)",
             "Rent sub-index (CPI 'Rent')", "Provincial / city CPI", "Years with full 12 months"],
    "Value": [cpi_path.name, cpi_meta["geography"], f'{cpi_long["measure"].nunique()} (incl. All-items, Shelter)',
              cpi_long["month"].min().strftime("%B %Y"), cpi_long["month"].max().strftime("%B %Y"),
              f'{cpi_long["month"].nunique()}', ", ".join(m.strftime("%b %Y") for m in missing_months) or "none",
              cpi_meta["base"], cpi_meta["release"].replace("Release date: ", ""),
              "NOT AVAILABLE — only the broader Shelter index is in the file",
              "NOT AVAILABLE — Canada-wide only",
              "none (2023 starts in April; 2025 ends in August)"],
})
print("Statistics Canada CPI file — coverage")
display(coverage_cpi)

# Year-over-year change by month, then the mean over the months available in each calendar year
wide = cpi_long.pivot_table(index="month", columns="measure", values="index")
yoy = (wide / wide.shift(12) - 1) * 100            # needs the same month a year earlier
cpi_summary = []
for y in [2023, 2024, 2025]:
    sel = yoy.loc[yoy.index.year == y, ["Shelter", "All-items"]].dropna()
    cpi_summary.append({
        "year": y,
        "months_with_yoy": len(sel),
        "shelter_yoy_pct": sel["Shelter"].mean() if len(sel) else np.nan,
        "all_items_yoy_pct": sel["All-items"].mean() if len(sel) else np.nan,
        "coverage": ("n/a — file starts April 2023, so no year-earlier month" if len(sel) == 0 else
                     f"{sel.index.min():%b}-{sel.index.max():%b} {y} only"),
    })
cpi_summary = pd.DataFrame(cpi_summary)
print("Canada-wide CPI year-over-year change (mean of available months)")
display(cpi_summary.round(2))

# ---- CMHC Rental Market Survey: load and document coverage -----------------
def parse_cmhc_table(path, sheet, header_row_hint):
    """Read a CMHC table; each bedroom column is followed by a reliability-letter column."""
    raw = pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=sheet, header=None)
    hdr = next(i for i in range(len(raw)) if str(raw.iloc[i, 0]).strip() == header_row_hint)
    headers = raw.iloc[hdr].tolist()
    body = raw.iloc[hdr + 1:].copy()
    names, last = [], None
    for h in headers:
        if isinstance(h, str):
            last = h.replace("\n", " ").strip()
            names.append(last)
        else:
            names.append(f"{last} (quality)")
    body.columns = names
    return body, str(raw.iloc[0, 0]), str(raw.iloc[1, 0])

def cmhc_number(x):
    return pd.to_numeric(str(x).replace("$", "").replace(",", "").replace("%", ""), errors="coerce")

urban_rent_path = find_file(["urban*average*rents*.xlsx"])
urban_vac_path = find_file(["urban*vacancy*.xlsx"])
rural_rent_path = find_file(["rural*average*rent*.xlsx"])
rural_vac_path = find_file(["rural*vacancy*.xlsx"])

urban_rent, urban_rent_title, urban_rent_ref = parse_cmhc_table(urban_rent_path, "CSD", "Province")
urban_vac, _, urban_vac_ref = parse_cmhc_table(urban_vac_path, "CSD", "Province")
rural_rent, rural_rent_title, rural_rent_ref = parse_cmhc_table(rural_rent_path, "Avg Rent_Province", "Dwelling Type")
rural_vac, _, rural_vac_ref = parse_cmhc_table(rural_vac_path, "Vacancy Rate_Province", "Dwelling Type")
for d in (urban_rent, urban_vac):
    d["Province"] = d["Province"].astype(str).str.strip()
urban_prov_codes = {"Que": "Quebec", "Ont.": "Ontario"}

coverage_cmhc = pd.DataFrame([
    {"File": urban_rent_path.name, "Measure": "Average rent ($)", "Geography": "Census subdivisions in urban centres 10,000+ (all provinces)",
     "Reference period": urban_rent_ref, "Grain": "bedroom type x dwelling type",
     "Years available": "2023 only", "Missing": "2024 and 2025 urban datasets not located; no year-over-year change or turnover-rent series"},
    {"File": urban_vac_path.name, "Measure": "Vacancy rate (%)", "Geography": "Census subdivisions in urban centres 10,000+ (all provinces)",
     "Reference period": urban_vac_ref, "Grain": "bedroom type x dwelling type",
     "Years available": "2023 only", "Missing": "2024 and 2025 urban datasets not located (not inferred)"},
    {"File": rural_rent_path.name, "Measure": "Average rent ($)", "Geography": "Province, centres of 2,500-10,000 people only",
     "Reference period": rural_rent_ref + " (month not stated in file)", "Grain": "bedroom type x dwelling type",
     "Years available": "2025 only", "Missing": "all other years. Small centres: NOT comparable to urban buildings"},
    {"File": rural_vac_path.name, "Measure": "Vacancy rate (%)", "Geography": "Province, centres of 2,500-10,000 people only",
     "Reference period": rural_vac_ref + " (month not stated in file)", "Grain": "bedroom type x dwelling type",
     "Years available": "2025 only", "Missing": "all other years"},
])
pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)

import unicodedata
def _norm(s):
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", str(s)).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode().lower().strip()

if "listings" in globals() and {"sBuilding", "sCity"} <= set(listings.columns):

- Ontario guideline 2023-2026: ontario.ca 'Residential rent increases' (official). Applies to most covered units; does not apply to units first occupied after 15 Nov 2018 or to a new tenant after turnover.
- TAL 2023 (2.3%), 2024 (4.0%), 2025 (5.9%): TAL's calculation example for an UNHEATED dwelling before major works, as reported by CBC / Centris / FADOQ (secondary sources). It is a reference calculation, not a cap or a minimum.

<h2 id="What-changed-from-2023-to-2025-in-the-rent-rules?">What changed from 2023 to 2025 in the rent rules?¶</h2><p>Québec — TAL rent-adjustment criteria. The TAL publishes percentages for components used in rent-adjustment calculations, such as electricity, natural gas, maintenance, building services, management costs and net income. The calculations use relevant CPI components for Québec and consider actual expenses for the building or dwelling. Capital expenditures are treated separately, using a reference interest rate plus 1%. The annual calculation tool considers expenses such as taxes, insurance, major improvements and operating costs. The published hypothetical examples are illustrations, not a guaranteed rent increase for every unit.</p> <p>The TAL's reference calculation for an unheated dwelling (before major works) was 2.3% for 2023, 4.0% for 2024 and 5.9% for 2025. The original notes list the TAL's reported average adjustments in cases brought before it: 3.1% for 2014–2022 in the 2023 announcement, 3.4% for 2015–2023 in 2024 and 3.8% for 2015–2024 in 2025 (these figures were not re-checked here). Those are historical averages from cases, not automatic annual increases. For 2026 the TAL moved to a new, simplified calculation method (in force since 1 January 2026); secondary sources report a 3.1% base percentage under it. The TAL percentage is guidance: in Québec a tenant may refuse an increase, and the landlord must then ask the TAL to fix the rent. The calculation applies to renewals; it does not set the rent of a new tenant after turnover.</p> <p>Ontario — annual rent increase guideline. The guideline was 2.5% in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025 and is 2.1% for 2026 (1.9% for 2027). For most rent-controlled units it is the annual maximum increase without Landlord and Tenant Board approval, with at least 12 months between increases and at least 90 days' written notice. It generally does not apply to units first occupied for residential purposes after 15 November 2018, or to a new tenant after turnover. Some exceptions and above-guideline increases apply.</p> <p>Why this matters for the forecast. Ontario's guideline is a regulated limit for most covered units, whereas Québec's TAL criteria are a calculation method, not a universal cap. Do not apply the Ontario percentage to Québec buildings or treat the TAL example as a fixed increase. In this data, most Ontario renewals (see the check below) rose by more than the guideline, which is consistent with The Met being an exempt, newer building but cannot be confirmed from the files provided.</p>

<h2 id="Limitations-and-what-the-estimate-is-%E2%80%94-and-is-not">Limitations and what the estimate is — and is not¶</h2>
  • Portfolio estimate, not an entitlement. The numbers are what this portfolio's own leases did in 2023–2025, projected forward with a simple rule. They are not a rent increase any landlord is entitled to charge, and not a maximum or minimum a tenant must accept.
  • Regulation limits what can be charged, and differently by province. In Ontario, for covered units, a renewal increase cannot exceed the guideline (2.1% for 2026) without Board approval; turnovers and exempt units are not bound by it. In Québec, the TAL percentage is a reference calculation: a tenant can refuse, and the TAL decides if the parties disagree. Turnover rents are not set by either rule. The unit-level legal status (exemptions, capital works, heating type, whether a unit is covered) is not in the data, so the notebook cannot say which units a rule applies to.
  • Contractual rent only. Concessions (free rent, parking, promotional credits) are not netted out. Effective-rent growth could differ, mostly for turnovers.
  • Small and thin groups. Ontario has pairs only from 2024 (two years, 95 turnovers and 130 renewals). Ontario cannot be backtested. Quebec results are far better supported (hundreds of pairs per year).
  • Backtest sample is three test years. Growth was below the prior-years average in 2023 and far above it in 2025, so a rule based on recent history over-predicted and then under-predicted. In this backtest the new equal-year method did not beat the old pooled median, and the prior low–high range contained the actual value in only some years. Three test years are too few to rank methods with confidence.
  • Missing external data. CPI covers Canada only, April 2023–August 2025, with no rent sub-index, no provincial split and no year-over-year for 2023. CMHC urban data is October 2023 only and rural data is 2025 only (smaller centres). There are no CMHC year-over-year or turnover-rent series, so market growth cannot be compared directly. See the cells above for which cells are marked "not available".

<h3 id="Conclusion">Conclusion¶</h3>
  • Whole portfolio: the recent-history method gives a central 2026 same-unit growth estimate of 4.2% (yearly range 2.3–7.0%, n=1894).
  • Québec renewals: 4.0% (yearly range 2.6–6.4%, n=1004); Québec turnovers: 5.2% (yearly range 1.9–9.0%, n=665).
  • Ontario renewals: 4.6% (yearly range 3.0–6.2%, n=130); Ontario turnovers: 6.9% (yearly range 4.9–9.0%, n=95). Ontario rests on only two years of history and small samples.
  • How reliable: in the 2023–2025 backtest the whole-portfolio estimate missed by 2.0 percentage points on average (the old pooled median: 1.8; repeating last year: 2.6). The actual value fell inside the prior low–high range in only 1 of 3 years (0 of 3 for turnovers). Growth jumped in 2025, so the range understates the real uncertainty; use it as a rough planning band only.
  • What this is not: these are portfolio estimates, not legal entitlements. In Ontario the 2026 guideline is 2.1% for most covered renewals (exemptions and turnovers differ); in Québec the TAL percentage is a reference calculation a tenant may refuse. Any actual increase for a specific unit must follow the applicable rules and lease.
